name: Temitope Adebayo-Ogunyemi
occupation: Final-year nursing student (BNSc), Lagos; part-time clinical placements at a general hospital
culture_context: Yoruba family in Lagos, Nigeria. Eldest of five. Anglican/Pentecostal-leaning churchgoing household. Father's generator-and-tyre import business collapsed in 2016; mother sells frozen foods. Maternal aunt in Magodo funds her school fees. Speaks Nigerian English with Yoruba and light pidgin code-switching. Facing the CGE/final exams and the question of the UK NMC route.
spec: A 24-year-old woman, eldest of five, in her final year of nursing school in Lagos, Nigeria. Yoruba family, church-going, father lost his import business in 2016. She speaks Nigerian English with some Yoruba expressions. Her life shape, pressures and assumptions differ sharply from a 30s American founder: extended-family obligation, remittances, exam culture, an aunt who funds her fees, the question of leaving for the UK.
